docs.text: Driver MCP970x Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Microchip MCP9700, MCP9700A, MCP9700B, MCP9701 and MCP9701A analog temperature sensors, read through any MCU's ADC, with clip, noise and range checks. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that reads one ADC channel in millivolts; it does the rest: power-up timing, averaging, the clip, noise and range checks, and the transfer function in integers. Other linear active thermistor ICs with a first-order output (V = V0 + TC x T) work through an explicit Custom variant that you declare completely. Analog temperature sensor MCP9700 / MCP9700A / MCP9700B / MCP9701 / MCP9701A Microchip Measures -40 °C to +125 °C (+150 °C with the High option on the MCP9700 and MCP9700B); -10 °C to +125 °C for the MCP9701 and MCP9701A Output 500 mV at 0 °C and 10.0 mV/°C (MCP9701 and MCP9701A: 400 mV and 19.5 mV/°C), typical Accuracy ±4 °C (MCP9700, MCP9701), ±2 °C (A grade), ±1 °C (MCP9700B, +20 °C to +70 °C), by temperature span Supply 2.3 V to 5.5 V (3.1 V to 5.5 V for the MCP9701 and MCP9701A), 6 µA typical Interface One analog output (VOUT) to an MCU ADC channel; the supply may come from an MCU pin (optional hook) What you get ¶ One object per sensor , no I/O until EnsureInitialized() . See API guide . The whole family as data : one variant table, no branch on a part name, plus the explicit Custom variant. See Configuration . Integers only : milli-degrees and millivolts, with one optional ToCelsius() for printing. See Transfer function . A reading you can trust : dummy conversions, averaging, clip ( Saturated ), noise ( Unstable ) and range ( OutputLow , OutputHigh ) checks, never a retry and never a clamp. See Architecture . Errors you can act on : Result<T> with an Error . See Contract . Zero-overhead portability : a CRTP port checked by a concept, one required hook for the ADC. See Porting . Tested without hardware against an independent model of the sensor and the ADC, and fuzzed. See Testing and CI . What a bench still has to confirm is in Limitations . docs.text: API guide ¶ The driver's API by task, with code that compiles. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Microchip Technology Inc. DS20001942 L: Shutdown from an I/O pin: 4.2 Shutdown Using Microcontroller I/O Pin, p. 11 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Group Calls Lifecycle EnsureInitialized() , IsInitialized() , Deinitialize() , Sleep() Measurement ReadMeasurement() , ReadTemperatureMilliC() , ReadOutputMv() Bring-up ReadRawPortMv() , GetLastRawPortMv() Information GetConfig() , GetSpec() , ResolutionMilliC() Free functions Validate() , ResolveSpec() , OutputMvToMilliC() , MilliCToOutputMv() , AccuracyLimitsFor() , ToCelsius() , ToString() Presets ConfigFor() , FastPreset() , LowNoisePreset() , Mcp9701Preset() , HighTemperaturePreset() The constructor stores the port and the configuration ( Config{} unless you pass one) and does no I/O. EnsureInitialized() is the one way to start the sensor: its first call checks the configuration, then starts it as the Contract page describes; once it has succeeded, later calls return Ok at once with no I/O, and after a failure the next call starts again from the beginning. No other call starts the sensor: before EnsureInitialized() succeeds every read returns NotInitialized . Deinitialize() , then EnsureInitialized() , is the recovery after a fault. Read the temperature ¶ #include "mcp9700.hpp" int read_board_temperature ( MyPort & port , int32_t & milli_celsius ) { mcp9700 :: MCP9700 < MyPort > sensor ( port ); // no I/O yet: an MCP9700 on a 12 bit, 3.3 V ADC if ( auto r = sensor . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. ADC up, settle, one validated reading return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // DeviceIdMismatch: wrong channel or no sensor } const auto t = sensor . ReadTemperatureMilliC (); // 2. discard 1, average 8, check, convert if ( ! t ) { return static_cast < int > ( t . error ); // OutputLow, OutputHigh, Saturated, Unstable or Bus } milli_celsius = t . value ; // 3. 25000 is 25.000 C return 0 ; } ReadTemperatureMilliC() returns milli-degrees Celsius (25000 is 25.000 °C), after the calibration offset. The result is an int32_t ; print it with integer arithmetic, or call ToCelsius() once if a float suits you. The whole measurement ¶ ReadMeasurement() returns the temperature, the mean voltage at VOUT and the spread of the conversions in one call. That is the call to use when you log the voltage next to the temperature or watch the noise: bool PrintableTemperature ( MyPort & port , int32_t & whole , int32_t & thousandths ) { Sensor sensor ( port ); if ( ! sensor . EnsureInitialized (). ok ()) { return false ; } const auto m = sensor . ReadMeasurement (); // temperature, mean VOUT and spread in one call if ( ! m . ok ()) { return false ; } const int32_t mc = m . value . temperature_mc ; whole = mc / 1000 ; // integer maths: no float needed thousandths = (( mc < 0 ) ? - mc : mc ) % 1000 ; return true ; } Calibrate ¶ mcp9700 :: Config CalibratedConfig () { mcp9700 :: Config c = mcp9700 :: LowNoisePreset (); c . channel = 2 ; c . variant = mcp9700 :: Variant :: Mcp9700B ; // the part on the board c . offset_cal_mc = -1200 ; // measured +1.2 C high at +25 C on this board return c ; } mcp9700 :: Error StartCalibrated ( MyPort & port ) { static Sensor sensor ( port , CalibratedConfig ()); // stored, no I/O return sensor . EnsureInitialized (). error ; // InvalidArgument if the config is out of range } Compare a reading with the datasheet ¶ AccuracyLimitsFor() returns the error the datasheet guarantees for your part at a temperature. The driver never applies it to a reading; it is for your own check, such as a production test against a reference: bool WithinDatasheetLimits ( const mcp9700 :: Config & c , int32_t reference_mc , int32_t reading_mc ) { const auto spec = mcp9700 :: ResolveSpec ( c ); if ( ! spec . ok ()) { return false ; } const auto lim = mcp9700 :: AccuracyLimitsFor ( spec . value , c . range , reference_mc ); const int32_t error_mc = reading_mc - reference_mc ; return lim . ok () && ( error_mc >= lim . value . min_mc ) && ( error_mc <= lim . value . max_mc ); } Switch the sensor off ¶ With an enable pin in the port, Sleep() powers the sensor down (a few µA less) and the next EnsureInitialized() powers it up again and waits for it. Without the pin, Sleep() returns Unsupported . Deinitialize() does the same and is also the recovery after a fault. If Sleep() or Deinitialize() returns Bus , the pin write failed: the sensor may still be powered, and the driver is uninitialised either way, so a second Deinitialize() does nothing. To retry the switch-off, call EnsureInitialized() (which switches the sensor on and checks it) and then Sleep() again; the order is covered by test_faults . Look at the raw ADC ¶ ReadRawPortMv() makes one conversion and returns the millivolts the port reported: no discard, no averaging, no check. Use it at bring-up to see what your ADC does; GetLastRawPortMv() returns the last conversion any read made. Handle errors ¶ const char * Describe ( mcp9700 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case mcp9700 :: Error :: DeviceIdMismatch : return "no plausible, stable output on this channel" ; case mcp9700 :: Error :: OutputLow : return "grounded or open input, unpowered sensor, wrong channel" ; case mcp9700 :: Error :: OutputHigh : return "shorted to the supply, or the ADC scale is wrong" ; case mcp9700 :: Error :: Saturated : return "the ADC clipped: declare its real full scale" ; case mcp9700 :: Error :: Unstable : return "floating or disturbed line" ; default : return mcp9700 :: ToString ( e ); } } This analog driver never returns Timeout , Crc , Busy or DeviceFault : it has no bus protocol and no fault register. Its faults are OutputLow , OutputHigh , Saturated and Unstable . A failed reading does not uninitialise the driver, and no call retries: the next call is a new reading. Every value it returns is on the Contract page, and the causes are in Troubleshooting .

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: the core, the port contract, and your port; and what one reading does. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Microchip Technology Inc. DS20001942 L: Output voltage range and an output outside it: 3.2 Output Voltage Pin (VOUT), p. 9 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into transfers (or, for an analog part, conversion requests) and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/mcp9700.hpp public calls ; inc/mcp9700_adc_interface.hpp AdcInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layer Files Owns Core inc/mcp9700.hpp , src/mcp9700.ipp Lifecycle, sampling, the clip, noise and range checks Types inc/mcp9700_types.hpp Error , Result<T> , Config , the variant table, the conversion functions, presets Compile-time helpers inc/mcp9700_detail.hpp Typed integer literals, exact hook probes, enumeration checks Port contract inc/mcp9700_adc_interface.hpp The CRTP base, CtrlPin , GpioSignal , the AdcPort concept, the output-load limits Platform port Your class ADC bring-up, calibrated conversions, delay, optional supply pin An analog sensor has no registers, so there is no register layer: the "chip definition" is the variant table, which is data (V0, TC, ranges, accuracy, packages) read by pure constexpr functions. A code path never asks which part it is; it asks the row. Variant::Custom builds a row from the user's declaration and uses exactly the same code. One reading ¶ One reading, step by step Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each card is one step of one reading. The driver first discards dummy conversions (an ADC multiplexer's sample capacitor still holds the previous channel), then converts N times with a wait between conversions and none after the last. The next steps look at those conversions together: a conversion within one ADC step of the declared full scale means the ADC clipped, a wide spread means a floating or disturbed line, and only then are the conversions averaged, scaled by the divider and turned into a temperature with the datasheet's transfer function in one integer expression. The window check compares that temperature with the specified range plus the margin; the calibration offset is added last. The red chips on the right are the one error each step can return; the first one that applies is returned, so a conversion that failed is Bus whatever else is wrong. Drawn from: src/mcp9700.ipp collect() ; src/mcp9700.ipp Evaluate() ; src/mcp9700.ipp ReadMeasurement() ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/read-pipeline.py . Discard. discard_conversions conversions whose value is thrown away. Convert. samples conversions, sample_interval_us between every two and none after the last. A failed conversion stops the reading at once with Bus : nothing is retried, and the conversions so far are dropped. Clip check. If the largest conversion plus one ADC step reaches the declared full scale, the ADC clipped: Saturated . The sensor's own output is far below any sensible full scale, so a clip is always a fault. Noise check. If the largest minus the smallest conversion, scaled to VOUT, exceeds max_spread_mv : Unstable . A floating input does this. Scale and convert. The mean, the divider and the transfer function are one integer expression, with one rounding at the end ( Transfer function ). Window check. The temperature against the specified range plus the margin: OutputLow or OutputHigh . Calibrate. offset_cal_mc is added to the temperature; the window check has already passed. The first failing check is the error: Bus beats Saturated , which beats Unstable , which beats OutputLow and OutputHigh . The order matters: a clipped conversion has no meaningful spread, and a floating line has no meaningful temperature. Start-up ¶ EnsureInitialized() resolves the variant row, brings the port's ADC up, switches the sensor on if the port can, waits power_on_settle_us and takes one validated reading. The reading is a weak analogue of a chip-ID check: a plausible, stable, unclipped output on the channel rules out a dead, grounded or rail-high line, but a floating pin that holds a stable mid-scale level passes too (see Limitations ). If it fails, the sensor is switched off again (best effort), the driver stays uninitialised, and the reason is logged and mapped to DeviceIdMismatch (or Bus when a conversion or the port failed). A failed write of the supply pin also ends in a best-effort switch-off, because the write may have powered the sensor. Next: Contract .

docs.text: Contract ¶ What the MCP970x driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Microchip Technology Inc. DS20001942 L: Output voltage range and an output outside it: 3.2 Output Voltage Pin (VOUT), p. 9 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() checks the configuration first ( InvalidArgument means nothing was sent), brings the ADC up, powers the sensor when the port has GpioSet() , waits power_on_settle_us and takes one validated reading. It is the only start-up call, and after it has succeeded it returns Ok with no I/O. Every call that touches the sensor returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds, and again after Deinitialize() or Sleep() , with no conversion and no pin write. No call starts the sensor as a side effect. A reading sends exactly discard_conversions + samples conversions, waits sample_interval_us between them and after none, and never retries. A reading is never clamped: a value outside the window is an error, not a limited temperature. A failed reading does not uninitialise the driver; a failed start-up leaves it uninitialised, with the sensor switched off again when the port has GpioSet() , and the next EnsureInitialized() starts again. Every port failure propagates as Error::Bus . A failed call returns a zero value. ReadRawPortMv() sends one conversion, and returns what the port gave: no scaling, no check, no retry. The sensor is driven INACTIVE (unpowered) by Deinitialize() and Sleep() , and ACTIVE only by EnsureInitialized() . Every log line is non-empty plain text, never a format string. Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates mcp9700_version.h Your port The ADC in millivolts, the delay, optionally the supply pin and a log Threading ¶ Not thread-safe; takes no lock. One owner task, or one mutex around every call. Errors ¶ Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 Before EnsureInitialized() succeeded, or after Deinitialize() or Sleep() InvalidArgument 2 Validate() failed at EnsureInitialized() ; nothing was sent Bus 3 The port's ADC bring-up, a conversion or a pin write failed Timeout 4 Never returned DeviceIdMismatch 5 Start-up found no plausible, stable, unclipped output on the channel Crc 6 Never returned Busy 7 Never returned DeviceFault 8 Never returned Unsupported 9 Sleep() on a port without GpioSet() OutputLow 16 The temperature is below the specified range minus the margin OutputHigh 17 The temperature is above the specified range plus the margin Saturated 18 A conversion is within one ADC step of the declared full scale, or above it Unstable 19 The conversions of one reading differ by more than max_spread_mv The base set keeps its values 0 to 9; the four chip-specific values start at 16, and each is returned by a call the tests make. Timeout , Crc , Busy and DeviceFault stay in the enumeration so a port can share one error type across drivers, and a test asserts that this driver never returns them. docs.text: The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() checks the configuration first ( InvalidArgument means nothing was sent), brings the ADC up, powers the sensor when the port has GpioSet() , waits power_on_settle_us and takes one validated reading. It is the only start-up call, and after it has succeeded it returns Ok with no I/O. Every call that touches the sensor returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds, and again after Deinitialize() or Sleep() , with no conversion and no pin write. No call starts the sensor as a side effect. A reading sends exactly discard_conversions + samples conversions, waits sample_interval_us between them and after none, and never retries. A reading is never clamped: a value outside the window is an error, not a limited temperature. A failed reading does not uninitialise the driver; a failed start-up leaves it uninitialised, with the sensor switched off again when the port has GpioSet() , and the next EnsureInitialized() starts again. Every port failure propagates as Error::Bus . A failed call returns a zero value. ReadRawPortMv() sends one conversion, and returns what the port gave: no scaling, no check, no retry. The sensor is driven INACTIVE (unpowered) by Deinitialize() and Sleep() , and ACTIVE only by EnsureInitialized() . Every log line is non-empty plain text, never a format string.

Parameter Value Page In the driver Output range over the specified range 100 mV to 1.75 V (MCP9700 family), 200 mV to 3 V (MCP9701 family) 9 the window of OutputLow and OutputHigh Output current 100 µA at most 4 kMaxOutputCurrentUa Output impedance 20 Ω typical, at 100 µA and 500 Hz 4 kOutputImpedanceOhm Output load regulation 2 Ω typical, 0 to +70 °C, 100 µA 4 not used by the code Load capacitance 1000 pF (characterised and production tested) 4 kMaxLoadCapacitancePf Nonlinearity ±0.5 °C typical, 0 to +70 °C 4 left in the result ( Limitations ) Line regulation 0.1 °C/V typical 3 not corrected Operating current 6 µA typical, 12 µA maximum (15 µA at +150 °C) 3 not used by the code Turn-on time t ON 800 µs typical, no maximum 4 Config::power_on_settle_us , default 2400 µs Thermal response t RES 1.3 s (SC70 on a 1 x 1 inch board), 1.65 s (TO-92 in a fluid bath), to 63 % 4 caps the averaging window The output is not ratiometric to VDD: a 0.1 °C/V line regulation means the supply barely moves the reading, so the driver needs the voltage at VOUT and nothing about the supply. An ADC that measures against its own supply does not change that, as long as its port reports calibrated millivolts. The datasheet does not give the output level of an unpowered or shut-down sensor, so the driver never relies on it. EnsureInitialized() waits for the turn-on time and then checks the first reading; a sensor that is still off reads as OutputLow or Unstable . The bench step to learn what your board shows is in Troubleshooting . The ADC in front of it ¶ The driver needs two numbers from you: the full scale of your port (the largest millivolt value it reports) and its resolution in bits ( Config::adc_full_scale_mv , Config::adc_resolution_bits ). docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( mcp9700_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-mcp9700.git external/driver-mcp9700 git submodule update --init external/driver-mcp9700 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-mcp9700 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE mcp9700::mcp9700 ) mcp9700::mcp9700 is an alias of the mcp9700 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect MCP9700_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver MCP9700_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-mcp9700 -B build-mcp9700 cmake --install build-mcp9700 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( mcp9700 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE mcp9700::mcp9700 ) The target is mcp9700::mcp9700 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated mcp9700_version.h go to include/mcp9700/inc/ , the template implementation to include/mcp9700/src/mcp9700.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-mcp9700) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-mcp9700 (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-mcp9700.git components/mcp9700 mcp9700 (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml mcp9700 (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : mcp9700 : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-mcp9700.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES mcp9700 (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/mcp9700_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into mcp9700_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = mcp9700 :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

bench item What it does not do ¶ No correction for nonlinearity, supply or self-heating. The result is the first-order equation of the datasheet; the error budget is on Transfer function . For better accuracy than ±0.5 °C typical after calibration, compensate with a table (the datasheet points to AN1001). No gain trim. One point calibrates the offset only. No detection of a floating pin that holds a stable level. A pin with no sensor that sits at a steady mid-scale voltage (a leaking ADC input, crosstalk, a held sample-and-hold capacitor) passes every check: 1650 mV reads as 115 °C on an MCP9700. A stuck-at-0 line ( OutputLow ), a rail-high line ( Saturated ) and a moving line ( Unstable ) are caught. On the board, add a 100 kΩ pull-down at the ADC pin so an open line reads OutputLow , or compare the first reading with a known temperature (O-14). The range window is a property of the part, so it cannot be narrowed to the climate of one product without a knob; range_margin_mc shrinks it. A grounded line is caught only below the window floor (20 mV or 49 mV by default, A-11). No detection of the part. The five devices cannot be told apart at run time; the declaration is yours. No detection of an ADC that is not what you declared. A full scale that is too high hides a clip. No power measurement. The operating current (6 µA typical) is a documented value, not a reading. No retries. A reading that fails is reported once; call again if you want another. Not thread-safe. One owner, or one mutex. Custom parts ¶ Custom serves another linear active thermistor IC whose output is first order. It is a declaration, not a verified part: no test can know your sensor. A wrong V0, TC or range gives wrong temperatures that look plausible. The two limits to know: 0 mV at the minimum (O-12). If V0 + TC x min is exactly 0 mV, a reading of 0 mV is a valid reading at the minimum, so a grounded or unpowered line is not caught by the window at any margin. Check at a known temperature at start-up, or add a pull-up on the board. Positive outputs only (O-13). A part whose output goes below 0 V at its minimum, or whose slope is negative, is rejected by Validate() . docs.text: Platforms ¶ The driver is MCU-agnostic: inc/ and src/ contain no SDK, RTOS or vendor header. A platform is three optional pieces around it, and only examples/<platform>/ holds platform code. Piece Where What it is Port examples/<platform>/ The class that implements the bus hooks for that MCU or OS ( Porting ) Example examples/<platform>/ A program that runs the driver there, built by CI Build integration the root CMakeLists.txt How that platform's build system finds the driver What exists today ¶ Platform Port Example Build integration Built by CI Host (Linux, macOS, Windows) examples/host/host_mcp9700_port.hpp (simulated chip) examples/host/ Plain CMake yes, run as a test ESP32 (ESP-IDF) examples/esp32/main/esp32_mcp9700_port.hpp examples/esp32/ Root CMakeLists.txt under ESP_PLATFORM (component) yes STM32, RP2040, nRF, other MCUs write one ( Porting ) none yet Plain CMake no Plain CMake ( add_subdirectory() or find_package() , see Installation ) covers STM32, RP2040, nRF and host builds. The root CMakeLists.txt also covers ESP-IDF: under ESP_PLATFORM it registers the repository as a component (a repository scaffolded without the ESP32 platform adds that branch back from the template when it needs it). Zephyr modules, Arduino library manifests and PlatformIO manifests are added only when a product needs them, and an example is added only together with a CI job that builds it. Add a platform ¶ The add-port skill has the details per MCU. In short: Create examples/<platform>/ with the port ( <platform>_mcp9700_port.hpp ), a small example program and a README with the wiring and the expected output. The folder is self-contained: it carries its own port and builds on its own. Build it in CI: a job in .github/workflows/ that builds the example, needed by the CI gate . A platform that CI does not build is not added. If its build system cannot use the root CMakeLists.txt , add the smallest manifest it needs, and say why in the pull request. Never put platform code in inc/ or src/ . Add a row to the table above and a page section if the platform needs one.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the port. It moves one millivolt value from your ADC and waits; the driver does everything else. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Microchip Technology Inc. DS20001942 L: Absolute maximum ratings: 1.0 Electrical Characteristics, p. 3 Output current, impedance and load capacitance: DC Electrical Characteristics (I_OUT, Z_OUT, C_LOAD), p. 4 Shutdown from an I/O pin: 4.2 Shutdown Using Microcontroller I/O Pin, p. 11 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver calls hooks on a class you derive from mcp9700::AdcInterface<Self> (in inc/mcp9700_adc_interface.hpp ). The base declares no hook; the driver template is constrained by the mcp9700::AdcPort concept, so a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error. What you implement ¶ Method Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept yes Bring the ADC up (unit, channel attenuation, calibration) on the first call; true at once afterwards bool ReadVoltageMv(uint8_t channel, uint32_t& voltage_mv) noexcept yes One conversion of channel , calibrated, in millivolts at the ADC pin ; false on any failure, leaving voltage_mv untouched void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept yes, for every wait Wait at least us microseconds bool GpioSet(CtrlPin, GpioSignal) noexcept no Power the sensor from an MCU pin; without it Sleep() returns Unsupported void Log(LogLevel, const char* message) noexcept no Print one line; message is plain text, never a format string ReadVoltageMv() is the standard millivolt hook of the Kokeb Labs driver contract, so one ADC port serves every analog-input driver. The driver asks for no raw counts and no reference voltage: you tell it the full scale and the resolution of your port in Config ( Configuration ). The port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyPort : public mcp9700 :: AdcInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the ADC up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_adc_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One conversion of `channel`, calibrated to millivolts. bool ReadVoltageMv ( uint8_t channel , uint32_t & voltage_mv ) noexcept { return platform_adc_read_mv ( channel , voltage_mv ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: power-up and sample spacing depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; A port with every hook: class FullPort : public mcp9700 :: AdcInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return platform_adc_init (); } bool ReadVoltageMv ( uint8_t channel , uint32_t & voltage_mv ) noexcept { return platform_adc_read_mv ( channel , voltage_mv ); } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: the sensor's supply from an MCU pin (DS20001942L Section 4.2). ACTIVE means // "powered". The pin idles INACTIVE until the driver enables it. bool GpioSet ( mcp9700 :: CtrlPin pin , mcp9700 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { if ( pin != mcp9700 :: CtrlPin :: Enable ) { return false ; } return platform_gpio_write ( kSupplyGpio , signal == mcp9700 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ); } // Optional: one line per failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( mcp9700 :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { ( void ) level ; platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } private : static constexpr int kSupplyGpio = 7 ; }; What the ADC must do ¶ Limit Value Why Input current 100 µA at most ( kMaxOutputCurrentUa ) The sensor sources and sinks at most that (I OUT , p. 4) Source impedance of the sensor 20 Ω typical ( kOutputImpedanceOhm ) An ADC with a large sample capacitor sees a small error after a switch Load capacitance 1000 pF ( kMaxLoadCapacitancePf ) The family is characterised and production tested with that (p. 4) Series resistor in VOUT none It adds an error with the input current; filter in the supply line instead (section 4.3) Return calibrated millivolts. If the SDK has a calibration (a curve fit for the ESP32, a factory gain and offset elsewhere), apply it in the port. If it has none, fail EnsureInitialized() rather than scale by a guess: a count scaled by a guess looks like a voltage and is not one. Declare the ceiling. On some MCUs the calibrated range at the attenuation you use ends below the supply (about 3.1 V at 12 dB on ESP32 parts). Put that value in Config::adc_full_scale_mv , not the supply: the clip check compares conversions with it. The ESP32 port keeps it as a constant next to the attenuation and asserts both at compile time. Multiplexed ADCs. The sample capacitor holds the last channel for a moment after a switch; that is what the driver's dummy conversion is for. If you give the sensor an ADC of its own, set discard_conversions to 0. Wait in DelayUs() . Power-up and sample spacing depend on it. A busy-wait is fine for the microseconds the driver asks; it never asks for more than a second at a time. Control pins ¶ The sensor may be powered from an MCU pin (section 4.2, p. 11), with 200 Ω in the supply line and 1 µF at the sensor (section 4.3; see Hardware ). Each control pin has a defined idle level, and the port drives it there before it enables the pin's output (handbook KB-HW-018): configuring a pin as an output first and setting its level afterwards can glitch the supply. CtrlPin Package pin Polarity Idle ( INACTIVE ) level Before the first read Enable VDD, through 200 Ω ACTIVE = powered (pin high) low: sensor off Set low, then enable the output; EnsureInitialized() powers it GpioSignal::ACTIVE always means "function asserted"; the port maps it to the electrical level. With an enable pin the driver gains Sleep() , and a failed start-up switches the sensor off again. Ports in this repository ¶ Port Where ESP-IDF: adc_oneshot with curve-fitting calibration, an optional enable GPIO, esp_rom_delay_us esp32_mcp9700_port.hpp Host: the simulated sensor and ADC host_mcp9700_port.hpp Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each driver object one owner task, or guard every call with one mutex.

If it has none, fail EnsureInitialized() rather than scale by a guess: a count scaled by a guess looks like a voltage and is not one. Declare the ceiling. On some MCUs the calibrated range at the attenuation you use ends below the supply (about 3.1 V at 12 dB on ESP32 parts). Put that value in Config::adc_full_scale_mv , not the supply: the clip check compares conversions with it. The ESP32 port keeps it as a constant next to the attenuation and asserts both at compile time. Multiplexed ADCs. The sample capacitor holds the last channel for a moment after a switch; that is what the driver's dummy conversion is for. If you give the sensor an ADC of its own, set discard_conversions to 0. Wait in DelayUs() . Power-up and sample spacing depend on it. A busy-wait is fine for the microseconds the driver asks; it never asks for more than a second at a time.

docs.text: The sensor may be powered from an MCU pin (section 4.2, p. 11), with 200 Ω in the supply line and 1 µF at the sensor (section 4.3; see Hardware ). Each control pin has a defined idle level, and the port drives it there before it enables the pin's output (handbook KB-HW-018): configuring a pin as an output first and setting its level afterwards can glitch the supply. CtrlPin Package pin Polarity Idle ( INACTIVE ) level Before the first read Enable VDD, through 200 Ω ACTIVE = powered (pin high) low: sensor off Set low, then enable the output; EnsureInitialized() powers it GpioSignal::ACTIVE always means "function asserted"; the port maps it to the electrical level. With an enable pin the driver gains Sleep() , and a failed start-up switches the sensor off again.

Datasheet sections this page relies on From Microchip Technology Inc. DS20001942 L: Pins and packages: Package Types; 3.0 Pin Descriptions, Table 3-1, p. 2 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . 1. Wire it ¶ MCU Sensor Notes ADC input VOUT The input must reach at least 2 V for an MCP9700 (1.75 V at +125 °C) 3.3 V VDD 100 nF to GND close to the pin; an MCP9701 or MCP9701A needs 3.1 V or more GND GND Same ground as the ADC reference The pin numbers depend on the package; Hardware has all three. Do not put a resistor in series with VOUT. If you want the driver to switch the sensor off, power VDD from an MCU pin through 200 Ω instead (see Hardware ). 2. Add the driver ¶ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-mcp9700.git external/driver-mcp9700 3. Write the port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyPort : public mcp9700 :: AdcInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the ADC up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_adc_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One conversion of `channel`, calibrated to millivolts. bool ReadVoltageMv ( uint8_t channel , uint32_t & voltage_mv ) noexcept { return platform_adc_read_mv ( channel , voltage_mv ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: power-up and sample spacing depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; The port returns millivolts at the ADC pin, calibrated. It does not return raw counts: the driver needs a voltage, and a count scaled by a guess is not one. 4. Read the temperature ¶ main.cpp #include "mcp9700.hpp" int read_board_temperature ( MyPort & port , int32_t & milli_celsius ) { mcp9700 :: MCP9700 < MyPort > sensor ( port ); // no I/O yet: an MCP9700 on a 12 bit, 3.3 V ADC if ( auto r = sensor . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. ADC up, settle, one validated reading return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // DeviceIdMismatch: wrong channel or no sensor } const auto t = sensor . ReadTemperatureMilliC (); // 2. discard 1, average 8, check, convert if ( ! t ) { return static_cast < int > ( t . error ); // OutputLow, OutputHigh, Saturated, Unstable or Bus } milli_celsius = t . value ; // 3. 25000 is 25.000 C return 0 ; } EnsureInitialized() checks the configuration, brings the ADC up, waits for the sensor to turn on and takes one validated reading, a weak analogue of a chip-ID check (it rules out a dead or grounded line, not a floating one). ReadTemperatureMilliC() discards one dummy conversion, averages eight, checks them for a clipped ADC, noise and an output outside the specified range, and applies the transfer function. 25000 is 25.000 °C. The defaults describe an MCP9700 behind a 12-bit ADC with a 3.3 V full scale. For another part or ADC, set the variant and the ADC's full scale and resolution in Config ( Configuration ): a wrong full scale hides a clipped reading. Next: API guide .

docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply ; --org names the organisation (a driver lives in kokeb-labs-drivers , everything else in kokeb-labs ) and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( adc analog temperature-sensor microchip mcp9700 ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> # the plan python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, Actions, labels, ... A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it again, with --check to see that nothing is pending, after the repository goes public (section 6). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ --apply in step 2 already creates them; this is the manual way, for a repository outside the org tool. python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md . 6. First release candidate and going public ¶ The order that works, and the reason for each step: main green first. Push, and wait for CI on main , including CI gate / gate . The docs publish to gh-pages from main before any tag does. Triage a failure with the release skill, section 5: re-run the failed jobs only when the infrastructure failed. Tag vX.Y.Z-rc.1 on that commit (the release skill). Its CI repeats the run, then the Release workflow publishes the pre-release: firmware, SBOM, checksums. A pre-release publishes its docs under its own tag and takes latest only when no other version holds it. Make it public ( gh repo edit <org>/<repo> --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences ), then python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply : rulesets, secret scanning with push protection, CodeQL and private vulnerability reporting need a public repository. If the last call answers 422, run it again after a few seconds; the new visibility has not reached that endpoint yet. Enable Pages from the gh-pages branch, root, and open https://<org>.github.io/<repo>/ . --check reports 0 change(s) pending . A private repository on the free plan shares a small Actions storage quota with the rest of its organisation. A full quota fails every upload step in every repository of it at once, which looks like a broken workflow and is not one; a public repository does not count against it.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against an independent model of the sensor and the ADC, a differential oracle, a fuzzer that controls what the ADC returns, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Nothing here touches a real sensor: see Limitations for what a bench still has to confirm. Host tests ¶ cmake -S . -B build -DMCP9700_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure The tests are written from the datasheet, not from the driver. tests/mock_mcp9700.hpp is a model of the sensor and the ADC in floating point with its own copy of the datasheet rows: the sensor (V0, TC, accuracy offset, nonlinearity, line regulation, turn-on time, an unpowered level), the ADC (full scale, resolution, offset and gain error, noise, clipping, channel-switch crosstalk, an external divider) and the faults (stuck low, floating, spikes, a failing conversion). tests/reference_mcp9700.hpp is a second, plain implementation of the driver's rules in 128-bit rational arithmetic; the differential tests and the fuzzer compare the driver with it. File Covers test_variant_table.cpp The table against the test's own copy of the datasheet, its invariants, the Custom rules at every boundary test_conversion.cpp OutputMvToMilliC() and its inverse at the datasheet reference points, rounding, against the oracle test_accuracy.cpp AccuracyLimitsFor() for every band, its edges and errors test_model.cpp End to end over the model: every named variant and synthetic Custom parts, swept across temperature test_validation.cpp Validate() one step inside and one outside every bound test_errors.cpp The base Error values; every chip-specific value is returned; the never-returned values stay unreturned test_lifecycle.cpp Construct, start, stop, restart; no traffic before start; the supply pin levels test_faults.cpp Each model fault maps to its error; bus failures; the precedence rule test_timing.cpp The settle wait, the sample intervals and the exact number of conversions test_calibration.cpp The offset is added after the window check test_boundaries.cpp The window edges to the millivolt, the saturation threshold, the spread limit, divider rounding, the Custom limits test_raw.cpp Single-shot raw access and the last-conversion getter test_kconfig.cpp KconfigDefaults() without Kconfig and with each variant's menuconfig values test_version.cpp The version getters follow the generated header tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( mcp9700_fuzz_mcp9700_corpus ), see below tests/compile_fail/ Ports and configurations that must not compile tests/docs/ Every code block on this site, compiled tests/check_install.cmake find_package(mcp9700) from an installed package The tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. The host example runs as a test too ( mcp9700_host_example ) and its output is part of the check. Fuzz tests ¶ Everything the driver reads is a voltage from the port's ADC, so the reading is what a floating input, a short or a wrong channel controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_mcp9700.cpp lets libFuzzer choose a configuration (sometimes invalid: any variant including Custom with random fields, a named variant with a stray custom field, a variant outside the enumeration), then up to 64 driver calls, and on every conversion what the ADC does: pass the model's output, fail, or return any 32-bit value. Between calls it can change the temperature, open the output, rewire the channel or power the sensor down. The port records everything the driver did in the last call, and after every call the target checks these promises against the oracle and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: ID Promise F1 A failed call returns an error this driver may return (never Timeout , Crc , Busy or DeviceFault ) and a zero value F2 Before a successful start, and after Deinitialize() or Sleep() , every call but EnsureInitialized() and Deinitialize() is NotInitialized with zero traffic F3 InvalidArgument means zero traffic, and happens only when the oracle rejects the configuration F4 A successful reading used exactly discard + samples conversions and the right waits F5 The error and the value equal the oracle's, recomputed from the recorded conversions F6 A success holds no conversion near the full scale and no spread above the limit: nothing out of range is ever Ok F7 ReadRawPortMv() sends one conversion and returns what the port gave; the last-value getter follows every conversion F8 Bus exactly when a conversion, the ADC bring-up or the supply write failed in that call F9 After a successful stop the supply was driven INACTIVE; a failed start switches it off; only EnsureInitialized() ever drives it ACTIVE F10 A failed start leaves the driver uninitialised; a second start after success is free F11 The waits of a successful start total at least the settle time, and none is longer than the longest knob F12 Every log line is non-empty plain text F13 No undefined behaviour for any input (UBSan with -fno-sanitize-recover=all ) F14 The named-variant, Custom and High rules agree with the oracle F15 A Custom start logs its one warning # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DMCP9700_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DMCP9700_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_mcp9700 ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_mcp9700 -max_total_time = 120 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_mcp9700 The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_mcp9700 , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_mcp9700/ on GCC and Clang ( mcp9700_fuzz_mcp9700_corpus ): the seeds ( custom-valid , custom-invalid , named-with-custom , not-started , init-and-read , bus-faults , config-invalid , stuck-low , float-high , saturated , unstable , power-cycle , mcp9701-high-temperature , max-samples-max-divider , raw-extremes ) and every input that ever broke a promise (name it regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request, from the seeds plus a corpus it keeps between runs (job Host quality / fuzz ). Quality gates ¶ The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise Measured for this driver (the gate output prints all three): lines 100 % (328 of 328), branches 99 % (226 of 227), conditions 99 % (209 of 210). The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DMCP9700_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DMCP9700_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( mcp9700_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/mcp9700.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published. CI workflows ¶ Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml with the repository root as the driver's component. The gate needs it too.

File Covers test_variant_table.cpp The table against the test's own copy of the datasheet, its invariants, the Custom rules at every boundary test_conversion.cpp OutputMvToMilliC() and its inverse at the datasheet reference points, rounding, against the oracle test_accuracy.cpp AccuracyLimitsFor() for every band, its edges and errors test_model.cpp End to end over the model: every named variant and synthetic Custom parts, swept across temperature test_validation.cpp Validate() one step inside and one outside every bound test_errors.cpp The base Error values; every chip-specific value is returned; the never-returned values stay unreturned test_lifecycle.cpp Construct, start, stop, restart; no traffic before start; the supply pin levels test_faults.cpp Each model fault maps to its error; bus failures; the precedence rule test_timing.cpp The settle wait, the sample intervals and the exact number of conversions test_calibration.cpp The offset is added after the window check test_boundaries.cpp The window edges to the millivolt, the saturation threshold, the spread limit, divider rounding, the Custom limits test_raw.cpp Single-shot raw access and the last-conversion getter test_kconfig.cpp KconfigDefaults() without Kconfig and with each variant's menuconfig values test_version.cpp The version getters follow the generated header tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( mcp9700_fuzz_mcp9700_corpus ), see below tests/compile_fail/ Ports and configurations that must not compile tests/docs/ Every code block on this site, compiled tests/check_install.cmake find_package(mcp9700) from an installed package The tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. The host example runs as a test too ( mcp9700_host_example ) and its output is part of the check.

docs.text: Everything the driver reads is a voltage from the port's ADC, so the reading is what a floating input, a short or a wrong channel controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_mcp9700.cpp lets libFuzzer choose a configuration (sometimes invalid: any variant including Custom with random fields, a named variant with a stray custom field, a variant outside the enumeration), then up to 64 driver calls, and on every conversion what the ADC does: pass the model's output, fail, or return any 32-bit value. Between calls it can change the temperature, open the output, rewire the channel or power the sensor down. The port records everything the driver did in the last call, and after every call the target checks these promises against the oracle and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: ID Promise F1 A failed call returns an error this driver may return (never Timeout , Crc , Busy or DeviceFault ) and a zero value F2 Before a successful start, and after Deinitialize() or Sleep() , every call but EnsureInitialized() and Deinitialize() is NotInitialized with zero traffic F3 InvalidArgument means zero traffic, and happens only when the oracle rejects the configuration F4 A successful reading used exactly discard + samples conversions and the right waits F5 The error and the value equal the oracle's, recomputed from the recorded conversions F6 A success holds no conversion near the full scale and no spread above the limit: nothing out of range is ever Ok F7 ReadRawPortMv() sends one conversion and returns what the port gave; the last-value getter follows every conversion F8 Bus exactly when a conversion, the ADC bring-up or the supply write failed in that call F9 After a successful stop the supply was driven INACTIVE; a failed start switches it off; only EnsureInitialized() ever drives it ACTIVE F10 A failed start leaves the driver uninitialised; a second start after success is free F11 The waits of a successful start total at least the settle time, and none is longer than the longest knob F12 Every log line is non-empty plain text F13 No undefined behaviour for any input (UBSan with -fno-sanitize-recover=all ) F14 The named-variant, Custom and High rules agree with the oracle F15 A Custom start logs its one warning # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DMCP9700_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DMCP9700_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_mcp9700 ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_mcp9700 -max_total_time = 120 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_mcp9700 The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_mcp9700 , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_mcp9700/ on GCC and Clang ( mcp9700_fuzz_mcp9700_corpus ): the seeds ( custom-valid , custom-invalid , named-with-custom , not-started , init-and-read , bus-faults , config-invalid , stuck-low , float-high , saturated , unstable , power-cycle , mcp9701-high-temperature , max-samples-max-divider , raw-extremes ) and every input that ever broke a promise (name it regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request, from the seeds plus a corpus it keeps between runs (job Host quality / fuzz ).

docs.text: The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise Measured for this driver (the gate output prints all three): lines 100 % (328 of 328), branches 99 % (226 of 227), conditions 99 % (209 of 210). The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DMCP9700_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DMCP9700_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( mcp9700_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/mcp9700.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published.

docs.text: Transfer function ¶ How a voltage at VOUT becomes a temperature: the datasheet's equation, the integer arithmetic the driver uses, the numbers at the ends of each range and what limits the accuracy of the result. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Microchip Technology Inc. DS20001942 L: Accuracy of each device: DC Electrical Characteristics, Sensor Accuracy, p. 3 Transfer function: V0 and TC of each device: 4.0 Applications Information, Equation 4-1; DC Electrical Characteristics, p. 10 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The equation ¶ The sensor measures the die temperature with a diode and scales it to a voltage (Equation 4-1, p. 10): V OUT = T C x T A + V 0 °C Family V0 at 0 °C TC Source MCP9700, MCP9700A, MCP9700B 500 mV 10.0 mV/°C DC Electrical Characteristics, p. 3 and p. 4 MCP9701, MCP9701A 400 mV 19.5 mV/°C the same tables The values are typical; the datasheet gives no minimum or maximum for either, only the accuracy of the result (below). The datasheet's note 3 on p. 3 points at "Equation 4-2" for the first-order equation, but Equation 4-2 is the self-heating equation: the transfer function is Equation 4-1. The driver follows Equation 4-1. Output voltage against temperature Figure description and sources The horizontal axis is the die temperature, the vertical axis the voltage at VOUT, from Equation 4-1, V = V0 + TC x T. The MCP9700, MCP9700A and MCP9700B share the lower line (500 mV at 0 C, 10.0 mV/C); the MCP9701 and MCP9701A the steeper one (400 mV at 0 C, 19.5 mV/C). The dashed line is a Custom example from the Configuration page. Each line is solid over its specified temperature range and dotted over the plausibility margin the driver adds on each side (range_margin_mc, default 8 C): a reading outside the solid part and its dotted margin is OutputLow or OutputHigh, never a temperature. The dots mark the ends of the specified range and the voltage there. Drawn from: inc/mcp9700_types.hpp kVariantTable ; inc/mcp9700_types.hpp range_margin_mc ; tests/docs/configuration.cpp custom-offset ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/transfer-function.py . The arithmetic ¶ The driver works in integers only: temperatures in milli-degrees ( _mc ), voltages in millivolts ( _mv ) and the slope in microvolts per degree ( _uv_per_c ). Solving Equation 4-1 for the temperature, with the mean output V in millivolts: T_mc = round( (V_mv - V0_mv) x 1000000 / TC_uv_per_c ) The mean, the divider and the equation are one integer expression with a single rounding at the end (half away from zero), so averaging eight conversions never adds a rounding step. It is evaluated in 64 bits. The reverse, MilliCToOutputMv() , rounds to the nearest millivolt and returns 0 for a temperature whose output would be negative. Temperature MCP9700 family MCP9701 family -40 °C 100 mV (below range) -10 °C 400 mV 205 mV 0 °C 500 mV 400 mV +25 °C 750 mV 887.5 mV +85 °C 1350 mV 2057.5 mV +125 °C 1750 mV 2837.5 mV +150 °C (High) 2000 mV (no High option) Datasheet p. 9 gives the output ranges as 100 mV to 1.75 V (MCP9700 family) and 200 mV to 3 V (MCP9701 family); the second is rounded: 205 mV and 2837.5 mV are the exact ends of -10 °C and +125 °C. The window of OutputLow and OutputHigh is the specified range plus range_margin_mc on each side (default 8 °C): for an MCP9700 that is -48 °C to +133 °C, 20 mV to 1830 mV (2080 mV with the High option). The margin is the datasheet's worst-case +6 °C error plus 2 °C of ADC error (open question A-4); see Configuration . ToCelsius() converts milli-degrees to a float for printing. It is the only floating-point in the driver; the result of every call is an integer. The error budget ¶ The reading is the sensor's error plus the ADC's, and the driver reports the sum without correcting for either: Source Size Where it is described Sensor accuracy ±1 °C to ±4 °C by grade and span, at VDD = 3.3 V (MCP9700 family) or 5.0 V (MCP9701 family) Hardware , AccuracyLimitsFor() Nonlinearity ±0.5 °C typical, 0 to +70 °C not corrected; Limitations Line regulation 0.1 °C per volt away from the tested supply not corrected; Limitations Self-heating 0.179 °C at the worst case, 25 °C not corrected ADC step ResolutionMilliC() , 81 m°C for a 12-bit 3.3 V ADC on a 10 mV/°C part Hardware ADC offset and gain whatever your ADC has; calibrated millivolts remove most of it your port Noise averaged away by samples ; flagged by max_spread_mv Configuration When a part is off by a fixed amount, measure it once at a known temperature and set offset_cal_mc : a one-point calibration at +25 °C improves the accuracy to about ±0.5 °C from 0 to +70 °C (section 4.1, p. 10), and the datasheet notes that a relative change from the calibration point is accurate to the same degree. A calibration at one point cannot fix the slope; a gain trim is not part of this version ( Limitations ).

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms, causes and fixes, cheapest check first. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Microchip Technology Inc. DS20001942 L: Output voltage range and an output outside it: 3.2 Output Voltage Pin (VOUT), p. 9 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Start with ReadRawPortMv() : it makes one conversion with no checks, so the number it returns is what your ADC sees. Compare it with a multimeter on VOUT. If they differ, the problem is the port or the wiring, not the driver. Symptom Likely cause Fix EnsureInitialized() returns InvalidArgument Validate() failed: a field out of range, a named variant with a custom field set, High on a part without it, an incomplete Custom Call mcp9700::Validate(config) and compare with Configuration ; nothing was sent EnsureInitialized() returns Bus The port's ADC bring-up, a conversion or the supply pin failed Check the unit, the channel and the calibration in the port; the log line names the step EnsureInitialized() returns DeviceIdMismatch No plausible, stable, unclipped output: the log line before it says which check failed See the four rows below OutputLow (or "start-up output too low") The sensor is unpowered, VOUT is grounded or open, the wrong channel, or the supply pin is not driven Measure VDD and VOUT; check Config::channel ; with an enable pin check the port drives it ACTIVE OutputHigh ("too high") VOUT shorted to the supply, a wrong variant (an MCP9701 declared as an MCP9700), or a mis-scaled ADC Check the part marking against Config::variant ; check a divider is declared Saturated ("at the ADC full scale") The ADC clipped: an open input pulled high, an attenuation too small, or a declared full scale that is too high Measure the pin; declare the port's real full scale; for a floating input fix the wiring Unstable ("unstable") A floating or disturbed line, a noisy supply, or max_spread_mv too small for your ADC Add the 100 nF at VDD (or 200 Ω and 1 µF); keep digital lines away; raise samples or max_spread_mv The first reading after a wake-up is wrong The sensor was not yet on Raise power_on_settle_us ; the datasheet gives no maximum turn-on time (p. 4) The temperature is a few degrees off The part's own accuracy (±1 °C to ±4 °C), the ADC's error, or a wrong variant Compare with AccuracyLimitsFor() ; calibrate once with offset_cal_mc ( Configuration ) The temperature follows the board, not the air The die is coupled to the PCB through the pins (section 4.4) Use the TO-92 package for air, or thermally isolate the sensor The temperature creeps up after a few seconds Self-heating, or heat from a nearby regulator An MCP970x at the maximum load self-heats 0.179 °C; look for the other heat source The temperature is wrong by a constant ratio A divider that is not declared, or the wrong adc_full_scale_mv Declare divider_num and divider_den ; compare ReadRawPortMv() with a multimeter Sleep() returns Unsupported The port has no GpioSet() Add it ( Porting ) ReadMeasurement() returns NotInitialized EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded, or Sleep() or Deinitialize() ran Call EnsureInitialized() and check its result A custom part reads 0 °C with the input grounded The part outputs 0 mV at its minimum, so 0 mV is valid Open question O-12 in Limitations Bench steps that confirm the assumptions ¶ These are not verified on hardware. Each one turns an assumption into a measured fact for your board. Unpowered output. The datasheet does not give the output of an unpowered or switched-off sensor (A-5). With the enable pin driven INACTIVE, read ReadRawPortMv() a few times, and write down the value and the spread. Then call EnsureInitialized() and confirm it succeeds only after the settle wait. Turn-on time. Power the sensor and read ReadRawPortMv() every 100 µs: the time until the value stops moving is your board's turn-on time. The default wait is 2400 µs, three times the 800 µs typical (A-1). Noise. Read 64 conversions with max_spread_mv = 1000 and look at Measurement::spread_mv : set max_spread_mv to about three times your board's quiet value (A-3). Clip level. Declare a full scale of 10000 mV, read a conversion with the pin tied to the supply, and write down what the port returns: that is the ceiling to declare (O-5). Floating pin. Disconnect VOUT and read: an input with no pull is Unstable or reads a leakage level, and a level that holds steady anywhere inside the window is accepted as a temperature (O-14). A 100 kΩ pull-down (about 7 µA at 750 mV, far below the 100 µA the output can source) makes an open line read OutputLow .

docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs kokeb-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. Inside the MCP9700 ¶ Inside the MCP9700 Figure description and sources The MCP9700's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/mcp9700.hpp ; inc/mcp9700_adc_interface.hpp . Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into transfers (or, for an analog part, conversion requests) and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The driver first discards dummy conversions (an ADC multiplexer's sample capacitor still holds the previous channel), then converts N times with a wait between conversions and none after the last. The next steps look at those conversions together: a conversion within one ADC step of the declared full scale means the ADC clipped, a wide spread means a floating or disturbed line, and only then are the conversions averaged, scaled by the divider and turned into a temperature with the datasheet's transfer function in one integer expression. The window check compares that temperature with the specified range plus the margin; the calibration offset is added last. The red chips on the right are the one error each step can return; the first one that applies is returned, so a conversion that failed is Bus whatever else is wrong.
